docs/platform/event-store/spec.md.sample: Store-layer completion (2026-10-20, dormant)
docs/platform/event-store/spec.md.text: ## Store-layer completion (2026-10-20, dormant)
docs/platform/event-store/spec.md.sectionText:
## Store-layer completion (2026-10-20, dormant)

The consumer registry remains empty. These store/facade operations do not wire
Work, porting or command lifecycle triggers.

- Append keeps the active-file, stream-directory and store-root durability barriers.
  The store root is synced on every append: an existing stream directory may
  have been created by a predecessor killed before its parent was synced. Recovery
  cleanup syncs the identity directory only after removing a temporary file.
  Repeated decoding reuses one thread-local verified frame only for exact bytes,
  origin, stream and strictness (at most 4 MiB of input); changed bytes always
  pass the full verifier. Reads still load the actual bytes.
- Inspect reuses Git's existing config cache and validates source stamps on each
  use. Authority and HEAD reuse is limited to the current read; ref/HEAD facts
  are never carried across commands.
- `store.maintenance(heldRanks)` returns local open-stream names and
  `oldestUnsealedAgeSec`, plus `lastPush` from the sync receipt. It uses no Git
  ref walk, worktree listing or legacy read, and runs outside hot gates. Full
  `status` remains the integrity/diagnostic operation. Future trigger consumers
  must use maintenance facts rather than full status. Age reads hold the append
  lock against recovery/truncation and rotation, open each file once and read only
  its first line, treating an incomplete first line as no age observation. The
  open handle retains the header snapshot across a concurrent sealing unlink;
  a file already removed by sealing is skipped. Later batch bytes are not parsed.
- `branchKey(branch, loaderOptions)` exposes the crate's single branch-key rule.
  `ownOrigin` is `null` when this clone has no local store identity yet (before
  its first append); otherwise it is the local origin string. Opportunistic seal
  and promotion are available on the facade;
  policy and lifecycle wiring remain consumer-owned.
- `read({cursor, folded, ...}, heldRanks)` forwards the supplied coverage and
  retained envelopes into the certified walk. A cursor without retained history
  cannot substitute for a lost view and still forces rebuild. Consumer cache reuse checks must
  compare only `cover`, `streams` and `deferred`, while refreshing certification
  and tip metadata from the returned cursor; these checks never replace the
  reader's fold/rebuild decision for changed foreign history.
- The pre-commit hook refuses staged added, renamed, copied and type-changed
  retired event paths using `--no-renames --diff-filter=ACRT`, **only when** the
  exact `.fgos/events` regular-file fence is in the index or HEAD. Without that
  fence, legacy shard/checkpoint commits keep their existing behavior. Enforced
  families are `.fgos/events.jsonl*` and `.fgos/events/`; unrelated prefixes are
  admitted, as is the exact fence path. Existing Work guards remain installed.

The store-increment benchmark uses the facade directly and its existing kernel
state gate, independently of a Work consumer. `--seed-items 1000` (the default)
seeds roughly 8 MB of payloads and seals them before measurement;
`--seed-history <jsonl>` instead copies explicit history records into benchmark
payloads without modifying the input. Every result records seed count, bytes and
source. Store-only numbers are not Work end-to-end acceptance. Ext4 latency,
power-loss qualification and the parked Work cutover remain separate gates.

The dormant branch's repository door test is a regression census, not evidence
that cutover V-DOOR-01 is complete: it asserts the exact pre-cutover invocation
and retired-reader findings as a shrink-only declared list keyed by file, call
kind and target family, with counts for distinct sites. It pins neither hashes
nor line numbers. Reader debt includes exact sites in legacy owner files rather
than exempting those files. New findings fail; removed findings must be removed
from the list. The generic scanner still returns those findings; E3 remains its
only fixture exemption class. WORK/Git caller cutover must remove these findings
before claiming the whole-repository zero-legacy gate.

docs/platform/event-store/spec.md.sample: Store read latency refinement (2026-10-20, dormant)
docs/platform/event-store/spec.md.text: ### Store read latency refinement (2026-10-20, dormant)
docs/platform/event-store/spec.md.sectionText:
### Store read latency refinement (2026-10-20, dormant)

The retained cursor records `verifiedTips`, exact ref-name/OID bindings from a
complete, undeferred read. Every new read observes the actual refs through Git
Inspect. Only a matching binding at a certified tip, with the same query and
retained history, can avoid reloading that tip's header. New names, moved refs,
lost history and deferred reads still verify the DAG; mirror rewind checks remain.
Old cursors without bindings take the verification path. Legacy reads reuse only
the current command's authority, HEAD and legacy-ref observation when discovering
and reading the old consumer roots. No driver-side HEAD/ref snapshot is reused across commands; cursor bindings are
cache keys checked against freshly observed refs.

The Node facade attaches an opaque native envelope-validation proof to each
returned sequence using a weak association owned by that consumer view. It is
neither a hidden current-state cache nor durable truth. Each supplied envelope is
compared in full with this proof; an edited or unrecognized envelope undergoes
normal hash validation. A copied, serialized or lost view works through ordinary
verification. Every call still reads local bytes and observes current Git refs
and HEAD. The native boundary takes retained JSON in one transfer and returns only
the sequence suffix after an exactly equal retained prefix; the facade returns
the same complete public sequence and fold decision as before.

The existing verified active-frame cache compares actual marker-closed prefix
bytes and decoding authority on every read, verifies the entire new/speculative
tail and checks sequence continuity across the boundary. Rewritten prefixes use
the full verifier. Its existing 4 MiB bound remains. Append retains all three
steady-state fsyncs and every initialization/recovery durability barrier.

The store benchmark advances its own cursor with `readInGate`'s tail before
append and records `outsideReadMs` for every mutation and outside-read p50/p95
per session count. Its 60-second limit and 50 ms p95 budget are unchanged. Host
acceptance still requires all 1/10/15/20-session rows; sandbox diagnostics do not
establish that acceptance. Work remains unwired.

docs/platform/event-store/spec.md.text:
The retained cursor records `verifiedTips`, exact ref-name/OID bindings from a
complete, undeferred read. Every new read observes the actual refs through Git
Inspect. Only a matching binding at a certified tip, with the same query and
retained history, can avoid reloading that tip's header. New names, moved refs,
lost history and deferred reads still verify the DAG; mirror rewind checks remain.
Old cursors without bindings take the verification path. Legacy reads reuse only
the current command's authority, HEAD and legacy-ref observation when discovering
and reading the old consumer roots. No driver-side HEAD/ref snapshot is reused across commands; cursor bindings are
cache keys checked against freshly observed refs.

docs/platform/event-store/spec.md.text:
The Node facade attaches an opaque native envelope-validation proof to each
returned sequence using a weak association owned by that consumer view. It is
neither a hidden current-state cache nor durable truth. Each supplied envelope is
compared in full with this proof; an edited or unrecognized envelope undergoes
normal hash validation. A copied, serialized or lost view works through ordinary
verification. Every call still reads local bytes and observes current Git refs
and HEAD. The native boundary takes retained JSON in one transfer and returns only
the sequence suffix after an exactly equal retained prefix; the facade returns
the same complete public sequence and fold decision as before.

docs/platform/event-store/spec.md.text:
The existing verified active-frame cache compares actual marker-closed prefix
bytes and decoding authority on every read, verifies the entire new/speculative
tail and checks sequence continuity across the boundary. Rewritten prefixes use
the full verifier. Its existing 4 MiB bound remains. Append retains all three
steady-state fsyncs and every initialization/recovery durability barrier.

docs/platform/event-store/spec.md.text:
The store benchmark advances its own cursor with `readInGate`'s tail before
append and records `outsideReadMs` for every mutation and outside-read p50/p95
per session count. Its 60-second limit and 50 ms p95 budget are unchanged. Host

docs/specs/reading-map.md.sectionText:
# Reading Map (sản phẩm)

> **Quy tắc chuyển tiếp hiện hành:** bắt đầu ở `docs/reading-map.md` và `docs/platform/README.md`
> (hoặc tra cứu nhanh tại `docs/transitional-switchboard.md`), rồi dùng mapping current-source tường minh của
> portal area. Không suy authority từ path, ngày review, độ chi tiết, hoặc
> riêng metadata `Canonical:`. Bảng kiểm chứng Phase 00 sống tại
> `plans/260925-documentation-authority-unification/current-authority-map-2026-09-25.md`;
> bảng đó không promote, migrate hay retire source nào. Phase 00 và Phase 01 đã
> hoàn tất; Phase 02–09 vẫn chưa được authorize.

- `docs/platform-foundations.md` — văn bản gốc 10 luật nền platform (L1–L10); spec: docs/specs/platform-foundations.md
- `docs/backlog.md` — product backlog (PBI rows, scribing-owned)
- `docs/architecture-map.md` — bản chuẩn kiến trúc (v0.2, record ADR0010 (bản đồ kiến trúc là bản chuẩn)): 5 tầng + 2 lớp phủ, sổ component + sổ contract (CTR001–CTR009), nghi thức thẻ-căn-cước-trước-code
- `docs/work-item-lifecycle-vision.md` — tầm nhìn nền tảng: chu trình sống của work-item (mixed-autonomy, base-workflow + domain-extension); khung cho các PBI STR14-STR18
- `docs/platform/packaging-distribution/README.md` — portal hiện hành cho packaging/distribution: `fgctl` bootstrap/init/repair/upgrade, workspace activation, doctor/fix readiness, legacy Node compatibility, skill/instruction projections. Khi mục này mâu thuẫn với `docs/specs/distribution.md`, đọc portal + implementation-alignment trước; `docs/specs/distribution.md` hiện là legacy/generated-curated source trong lúc migration.
- `docs/distribution-vision.md` — tầm nhìn nền tảng lịch sử: cài đặt/setup/doctor ổn định + tái dùng được (không cần clone, global/project không xung đột — project ghi đè global, doctor/setup tự fix hạ tầng + merge config thiếu, module mới tự đăng ký năng lực config, CI như một phần của setup); đã được promote/supersede từng phần vào `docs/platform/packaging-distribution/vision.md`.
- `docs/specs/` — state layer: area spec + system-overview + bản đồ này
- `docs/routing-handoff-contract.md` — hợp đồng handoff agent↔agent + ranh giới tin cậy
- `docs/io-contract.md` — hợp đồng giao tiếp VÀO/RA của cửa CLI + bề mặt stdout `fgos-runner` (str46-io-contract): danh tính `writer`/`role`, envelope `fgos.v1` + ngoại lệ có lý do, exit-code một nguồn, sổ verb (`touchesState`/`externalEffect`/`paginated`/`multiValueFormat`), version token, ranh giới ngoài (STR38/STR48/STR83)
- `docs/coexistence.md` — doctrine chạy cạnh một harness agent khác (record ADR0009 (chống giao thoa lúc cài — fgOS khi cài không giao thoa tiến trình với harness khác)): lãnh địa, một-nhạc-trưởng-mỗi-phiên, nhường-nhịn lúc `init`, manifest `.fgos/coexistence.json`, Known Gaps chưa flip; `src/install/coexist.mjs` — cài đặt detection + manifest (read-only, không đè)
- `package.json` (`version`, `files`, `bin.fgos`, `bin.fgos-runner`) + `README.md` (mục `## Install`) — cài `fgos` VÀ `fgos-runner` từ ngoài source repo qua GitHub install, cả hai executable ngay sau cài; `test/install-packaging.test.mjs` — proof e2e (pack → install → chạy từ project ngoài, gồm cả hai binary); spec: docs/specs/distribution.md
- `scripts/fgos-shell-integration.sh` — dev checkout shell helper (STR87 first slice): hàm `fgos`/`fgos-runner` tự resolve root qua `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (worktree-safe), source từ shell profile của contributor, không cài đặt gì; test: `test/scripts/fgos-shell-integration.test.mjs`; spec: docs/specs/distribution.md §Dev checkout shell helpers
- `src/setup/` (`ansi.mjs`, `config-merge.mjs`, `shell-rc.mjs`, `checks.mjs`) + `bin/fgos.mjs`'s current legacy `setup`/`doctor` verbs + `src/cli/command-registry.mjs` entries — doctor/fix registry and legacy setup compatibility: `doctor` chẩn đoán read-only, `doctor --fix` chạy registered fixes, current Node `fgos setup` vẫn tồn tại nhưng target architecture supersedes onboarding bằng `fgctl init` + local `fgos init` / `fgos doctor --fix` / `fgos doctor`; manifest: `docs/architecture-manifest.json`; test: `test/setup/*.test.mjs`; current portal: `docs/platform/packaging-distribution/README.md`; legacy spec: docs/specs/distribution.md §Setup, §Doctor
- `docs/decisions/` — hồ sơ quyết định dài hạn cho người ngoài (decision records); từ str64-backfill, mỗi record còn mang đầu-mô-tả OKF-style (loại/tiêu đề/nhãn/thời điểm/móc-liên-kết-nguồn, xem `frontmatter.mjs` dòng dưới) và được `fgos docs-index` công nhận là vị trí thay thế của ngăn `explanation` (R10, spec: docs/specs/enduser-docs-index.md) — thân ADR không đổi, chỉ thêm đầu-mô-tả; lưu ý `orchestrator` là pinned term đã đổi nghĩa giữa chừng (0026→0028 nghĩa cũ "launcher", 0029 nghĩa mới "tầng hợp thành T0"; xem chuỗi quyết định tại `docs/decisions/index.md` dòng 28-32)
- `scripts/check-decision-citation-drift.mjs` + `test/scripts/check-decision-citation-drift.test.mjs` — quét `docs/backlog.md` + `docs/specs/*.md` tìm dòng còn trích một quyết định đã bị supersede mà không nhắc quyết định thay thế trên cùng dòng (STR72 CoS clause 2, PBI p-2d71dfc3); chỉ phát hiện, không tự sửa; spec: docs/specs/decision-citation-drift.md
- `scripts/check-decision-codes.mjs` + `test/scripts/check-decision-codes.test.mjs` — quét `test/**/*.test.mjs` tìm tên test còn nhúng mã quyết định nội bộ (str##/D#/RUL##/STR##/tsk-xxx) thay vì mô tả bất biến bằng lời thường (review-audit-self-decision.md mục Stable Code Artifacts); chặn (ratchet) chỉ vi phạm MỚI so với `scripts/check-decision-codes.baseline.json` đã chốt, không chặn ngược nợ cũ; `npm test` tự chạy qua glob `test/**/*.test.mjs`, không hook riêng
- `docs/id-systems-audit.md` — audit + quyết định hình dạng mọi hệ id/mã đang sống trong hệ thống (work.id/kind/Story/ADR/Rule/Contract phía fgOS; D-hex/D-local/cell-id/feature-slug/severity phía bee) — nguồn cho `work.id`'s `tsk-<hash>` và các migration STR53-STR58 (tất cả đã `done`); boundary appendix: `docs/architecture-map.md` Phụ lục B
- `bin/fgos.mjs` — CLI một cửa của work-state; chạy `node bin/fgos.mjs <verb>`; gồm verb `edit` — sửa đè các trường (title/kind/risk/verify/tier/refs/deps/acceptance/priority/intent — str7-str8-priority-intent) trên một item đã có, cùng cửa ghi CTR002 như `add`/`move`; gồm verb `take`/`return` — cửa pull giao–nhận việc cho tác nhân ngoài runner; gồm verb `pick` — cửa pull GỘP `take` + dựng workspace (`createWorktree`), role cố định `session`, không cờ `--role` (theo str83-fgos-slash-commands); gồm verb `review`/`approve`/`reject` — cổng duyệt PR nội bộ, một cổng cho mọi đề xuất `awaiting-approval`, nay leaf-vs-root-aware (con nhập vào nhánh của gốc, gốc nhập vào cây chính); `review`/`approve` nay chấp nhận thêm `--github [--pr <n>]` — vận chuyển thay thế CÙNG cổng duyệt qua GitHub thay vì diff/merge cục bộ (chỉ nguồn runner, theo github-adapter, spec: docs/specs/runner.md); gồm verb `catchup` — đồng bộ lại một việc đỗ vì gãy nhập/trôi tích hợp (spec: docs/specs/runner.md); gồm verb `session` (`start`/`end`/`list`) — vòng đời phiên checkout đa-phiên tùy chọn, mỗi phiên một worktree detached-HEAD cho cây nguồn, dùng chung MỘT kho `.fgos/` qua symlink (spec: docs/specs/runner.md); spec: docs/specs/work-state.md
- `src/state/` — lõi work-state: events (nhật ký; `appendEvent` nay chạy trong mutex nóng `state` (`withStateTx`, `src/state/hot-lock.mjs`) — xem spec Work-State RUL10 (tiền đề có ngưỡng — một người ghi tại một thời điểm; multi-agent ghi đồng thời qua mutex nóng `state`)), work (schema — STATUSES + STAGES + field `parent` lineage + field `domain`), fsm (bảng chuyển status + CAS), stage (bảng chuyển stage + CAS, chiều vĩ mô song song fsm; cạnh chuyển-stage tra theo domain của item — `coding`: `discovery → exploring → planning → executing`, trong đó phán-quyết `clear` ở `discovery` bỏ qua `exploring` để sang thẳng `planning` còn `unclear` đi qua `exploring`; tên `decompose` vẫn còn nhưng chỉ là bí danh legacy chỉ-để-rút-cạn (không việc MỚI nào vào được nữa); `synthetic`: một stage, không cạnh nào), domains (sổ đăng ký domain — stage list + step-mapping base-workflow + cạnh-chuyển mỗi domain; `coding` + ba domain minh họa/thử-nghiệm `synthetic` (đúng một stage), `triage`, `fixture-marketing`; base-workflow-model STR18, hoàn tất S1+S2), replay (fold), frontier (truy vấn sẵn-sàng — lọc theo status, stage domain-aware, VÀ lineage qua `parent`), dep-graph (dò chu trình trên `deps` — bất biến phi-chu-trình tại cửa ghi, per work-graph-intelligence S1), store (chủ ghi duy nhất + readRawEvents), envelope (phong bì output CTR001, `wrapEnvelope` — nay bọc MỌI verb ở một cửa in trong `bin/fgos.mjs main()`, STR37; spec: docs/specs/work-state.md §envelope)
- `src/cli/command-registry.mjs` — sổ verb máy-đọc của CLI (STR37, kernel, thuần dữ liệu): `SCHEMA_VERSION` + `COMMAND_REGISTRY` (mọi verb với `{name, invoke, description, parameters, examples, access read|mutation, deprecated}`); `bin/fgos.mjs` `--help [--json]` và `<verb> [<sub>] --help [--json]` sinh sổ từ đây; verb có sub-verb mang `subcommands`, `HELP_SELECTORS` (`--help`, `-h`) thành route của Rust host qua `scripts/export-command-selectors.mjs`; test chống-lệch `test/cli/fgos-manifest.test.mjs`, `test/cli/subcommand-flag-drift.test.mjs` (cờ handler ↔ schema sub-verb), `test/cli/fgos-verb-help-json.test.mjs`, `test/rust-host/help-routes.test.mjs` (qua host thật); spec: docs/specs/work-state.md §sổ verb
- `src/intake/classify.mjs` — logic thuần của `fgos submit`: deriveTitle, classify (tier/kind/risk cơ học), generateId (`tsk-<hash>` chống trùng, STR53)
- `src/intake/discovery.mjs` — context-discovery của stage `discovery` (stage đầu tiên của domain `coding`): `resolveDiscovery` (đọc-phán-ghi, dùng chung bởi verb `discover` và vòng tự hành) ĐÒI phán-quyết do người gọi cấp — judge lồng `judgeDiscovery` đã rút; phán-quyết `clear` chuyển item sang stage `planning`, `unclear` sang `exploring`
- `src/intake/plan.mjs` — phán chia-việc của stage `planning`: `resolvePlan` (đọc-phán-ghi, dùng chung bởi verb `plan` và vòng tự hành khi item ở stage `planning`, hoặc ở bí danh legacy `decompose`) ĐÒI phán-quyết do người gọi cấp — judge lồng `judgeDecompose` đã rút, cùng lý do `judgeDiscovery` rút; sinh con qua lineage `parent`, không qua `deps`
- `domains/coding/AGENTS.md` `## fgOS Workflow` + `.claude/skills/` (`.agents/skills/` mirror byte-identical) — lớp hướng dẫn P50: entry skill (`fgos-routing`) + skill giai đoạn (`fgos-coding-discovering`/`fgos-coding-exploring`/`fgos-coding-planning`/`fgos-coding-validating`/`fgos-coding-implement`/`fgos-coding-knowledge`) trỏ một phiên tự mở tới đúng skill theo `stage` của item; từ str89-fgos-domain-skills, tra cứu này domain-pluggable — đọc trường `domain` + `stage` của item rồi tra qua `skillForStage`/`getDomain` (`src/state/workflow-stage-graphs.mjs`), không còn giả định ngầm domain `coding`; `fgos-routing` nay có hàng khoá theo **status** `retrospective → fgos-coding-knowledge` (skill tổng hợp cấp nhãn Diataxis + soạn tài liệu người-dùng-cuối) — stage `compound-learn` đã rút, việc tổng hợp nó từng canh nay là việc của status `retrospective`; skill ĐỘC LẬP `fgos-submit-assist` (str51-llm-assist-classify) đã rút (tsk-6ar) — `/fgOS:submit` bước 6 (`plugins/fgOS/skills/submit/SKILL.md`) nay tự chạy clarify+classify trong cùng phiên sống, cùng việc mà skill đó từng làm nhưng trên bản mô tả SẠCH hơn; spec: docs/specs/work-state.md §RUL60 (hành vi), docs/specs/runner.md (lớp hướng dẫn)
- `plugins/fgOS/` (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` + `skills/<verb>/SKILL.md`) — bề mặt slash-command `/fgOS:<verb>` cho Claude Code, 12 verb wrapper (submit, pick, move, return, ask, answer, ready, stale, rollup, check, graph, conflicts), mỗi verb một wrapper one-door-write qua `bin/fgos.mjs <verb>`; spec: docs/specs/fgos-plugin.md
- `apps/fgos-gateway/` + `apps/fgos-gateway/web/` — fgos gateway (REST, MCP, bundle web dashboard nhúng sẵn; vòng đời `fgos gateway`) và bề mặt web dashboard: client trình duyệt ĐỘC LẬP (không phải code máy chủ trong gateway, theo tsk-7l9 + decision 0014); `herdr-dashboard/` là plugin herdr (TUI trong pane), `packages/herdr-fgos-common/rust` là adapter CLI fgos dùng chung của cả hai, gọi API REST/RPC của gateway từ ngoài; ba màn đọc (taskboard, task-detail, câu hỏi cần trả lời — phủ cả kênh `ask` lẫn `gate-approve`) cộng các hành động ghi đi qua verb một-cửa-ghi của fgOS (`answer`/`approve`/`add`/`edit`/`move`), không có đường ghi thứ hai; bật mặc định, port 8788, token bắt buộc; spec: docs/specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md (lớp UI/wireframe: docs/reference/herdr-web-dashboard-layout.md)
- `docs/how-to/`, `docs/tutorials/`, `docs/reference/`, `docs/explanation/` — tài liệu NGƯỜI-DÙNG-CUỐI theo bốn quadrant Diataxis (audience-facing, khác `docs/specs/` là BA-reference nội bộ); sinh bởi kỹ năng `fgos-coding-knowledge` ở status `retrospective` (grow-or-create một tài liệu SỐNG mỗi đường dẫn: gom mọi capture qua `fgos doc-sources` rồi tích luỹ không mất, ngăn Diataxis là trục cấu trúc duy nhất — write-side, spec: docs/specs/enduser-docs-authoring.md), quadrant khớp `docType` capture; `docs/explanation/` từ str64-backfill còn có 6 tài liệu chưng cất từ critical-patterns.md (learnings vận hành bee thật sự thuộc tiến trình hình thành fgOS); chỉ mục đọc-theo-tag máy-đọc-được: `docs/enduser-docs-index.json` (sinh bởi verb `fgos docs-index` / kỹ năng `fgos-indexing`, thay cho việc liệt-kê-tay từng tài liệu — supersedes con trỏ văn xuôi cũ, theo compound-learn-enduser-docs; ngăn `explanation` còn quét thêm `docs/decisions/` làm vị trí thay thế, theo str64-backfill); spec read-side: docs/specs/enduser-docs-index.md
- `src/runner/` + `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` — vòng tự hành (loop/dispatch/worktree/recovery/anti-loop/write-queue/root-affinity); `loop.mjs`'s `runWatch` + `write-queue.mjs`'s `onCommit` — chế độ `--watch` bền, tín hiệu-cơ-học + nghỉ dự phòng, ghép `runOnce` không đổi làm hộp đen (str7-str8-priority-intent, spec: docs/specs/runner.md §RUL53 (`--watch` — vòng cầm-giao bền, dừng chỉ khi có tín hiệu tường minh)); loop giao việc theo mẻ song song có giới hạn hai tầng (cấu hình `parallel` trong `.fgos/config.json`'s `runner` section, theo tsk-5vf), giữ quyền-sở-hữu-gốc trong một lượt chạy, quét làm-rõ rồi quét chia-việc trước mọi dispatch thi công; gặt-lại bỏ qua claim của cửa pull (`claimRole` human/session); `dispatch.mjs`'s executor là port có tên CTR009 v2 (`EXECUTOR_ADAPTERS`, per-tier qua config's `executors`, STR41), `ensureRunnerConfigForDir` tự sinh cấu hình mặc định tại `.fgos/config.json` khi vắng mặt (không áp dụng cho `--config` tường minh, str76-runner-bootstrap; tsk-5hv xoá hẳn fallback về file flat legacy cũ); worker của loop và fan-out chạy như một Unit run qua `runUnit` (`work-dispatch.mjs`'s `spawnWorker`), `fgos-runner` không còn `--config` (spec: docs/specs/runner.md §RUL93 (the runner loop's worker and the fan-out batch run as one Unit run each)) và prompt worker được tách sang `prompt-templates.mjs` + `prompt-templates/*.txt` (chọn template qua bảng cơ học kind/tier/domain, substitution `{placeholder}` thuần, log dispatch kèm tên+hash template, STR49); `goal-check.mjs` — hàm goal-check dùng chung giữa vòng tự hành và verb `return`; `write-queue.mjs` — cửa ghi tuần tự giữ một-người-ghi dưới song song; `root-affinity.mjs` — quyền-sở-hữu-gốc, giữ mọi con của một gốc chung một chủ trong một lượt chạy; `resolveRepoRoot` nay còn xác nhận HEAD repo resolve được trước khi runner claim bất kỳ item nào (fail-fast, str86-runner-headless-git D ecfd0d1a); config: `.fgos/config.json`'s `runner` section (tự sinh khi vắng mặt tại đường mặc định, nguồn config duy nhất kể từ tsk-5hv); spec: docs/specs/runner.md

- `docs/backlog.md` — product backlog (PBI rows, scribing-owned)
- `docs/architecture-map.md` — bản chuẩn kiến trúc (v0.2, record ADR0010 (bản đồ kiến trúc là bản chuẩn)): 5 tầng + 2 lớp phủ, sổ component + sổ contract (CTR001–CTR009), nghi thức thẻ-căn-cước-trước-code
- `docs/work-item-lifecycle-vision.md` — tầm nhìn nền tảng: chu trình sống của work-item (mixed-autonomy, base-workflow + domain-extension); khung cho các PBI STR14-STR18
- `docs/platform/packaging-distribution/README.md` — portal hiện hành cho packaging/distribution: `fgctl` bootstrap/init/repair/upgrade, workspace activation, doctor/fix readiness, legacy Node compatibility, skill/instruction projections. Khi mục này mâu thuẫn với `docs/specs/distribution.md`, đọc portal + implementation-alignment trước; `docs/specs/distribution.md` hiện là legacy/generated-curated source trong lúc migration.
- `docs/distribution-vision.md` — tầm nhìn nền tảng lịch sử: cài đặt/setup/doctor ổn định + tái dùng được (không cần clone, global/project không xung đột — project ghi đè global, doctor/setup tự fix hạ tầng + merge config thiếu, module mới tự đăng ký năng lực config, CI như một phần của setup); đã được promote/supersede từng phần vào `docs/platform/packaging-distribution/vision.md`.
- `docs/specs/` — state layer: area spec + system-overview + bản đồ này
- `docs/routing-handoff-contract.md` — hợp đồng handoff agent↔agent + ranh giới tin cậy
- `docs/io-contract.md` — hợp đồng giao tiếp VÀO/RA của cửa CLI + bề mặt stdout `fgos-runner` (str46-io-contract): danh tính `writer`/`role`, envelope `fgos.v1` + ngoại lệ có lý do, exit-code một nguồn, sổ verb (`touchesState`/`externalEffect`/`paginated`/`multiValueFormat`), version token, ranh giới ngoài (STR38/STR48/STR83)
- `docs/coexistence.md` — doctrine chạy cạnh một harness agent khác (record ADR0009 (chống giao thoa lúc cài — fgOS khi cài không giao thoa tiến trình với harness khác)): lãnh địa, một-nhạc-trưởng-mỗi-phiên, nhường-nhịn lúc `init`, manifest `.fgos/coexistence.json`, Known Gaps chưa flip; `src/install/coexist.mjs` — cài đặt detection + manifest (read-only, không đè)
- `package.json` (`version`, `files`, `bin.fgos`, `bin.fgos-runner`) + `README.md` (mục `## Install`) — cài `fgos` VÀ `fgos-runner` từ ngoài source repo qua GitHub install, cả hai executable ngay sau cài; `test/install-packaging.test.mjs` — proof e2e (pack → install → chạy từ project ngoài, gồm cả hai binary); spec: docs/specs/distribution.md
- `scripts/fgos-shell-integration.sh` — dev checkout shell helper (STR87 first slice): hàm `fgos`/`fgos-runner` tự resolve root qua `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (worktree-safe), source từ shell profile của contributor, không cài đặt gì; test: `test/scripts/fgos-shell-integration.test.mjs`; spec: docs/specs/distribution.md §Dev checkout shell helpers
- `src/setup/` (`ansi.mjs`, `config-merge.mjs`, `shell-rc.mjs`, `checks.mjs`) + `bin/fgos.mjs`'s current legacy `setup`/`doctor` verbs + `src/cli/command-registry.mjs` entries — doctor/fix registry and legacy setup compatibility: `doctor` chẩn đoán read-only, `doctor --fix` chạy registered fixes, current Node `fgos setup` vẫn tồn tại nhưng target architecture supersedes onboarding bằng `fgctl init` + local `fgos init` / `fgos doctor --fix` / `fgos doctor`; manifest: `docs/architecture-manifest.json`; test: `test/setup/*.test.mjs`; current portal: `docs/platform/packaging-distribution/README.md`; legacy spec: docs/specs/distribution.md §Setup, §Doctor
- `docs/decisions/` — hồ sơ quyết định dài hạn cho người ngoài (decision records); từ str64-backfill, mỗi record còn mang đầu-mô-tả OKF-style (loại/tiêu đề/nhãn/thời điểm/móc-liên-kết-nguồn, xem `frontmatter.mjs` dòng dưới) và được `fgos docs-index` công nhận là vị trí thay thế của ngăn `explanation` (R10, spec: docs/specs/enduser-docs-index.md) — thân ADR không đổi, chỉ thêm đầu-mô-tả; lưu ý `orchestrator` là pinned term đã đổi nghĩa giữa chừng (0026→0028 nghĩa cũ "launcher", 0029 nghĩa mới "tầng hợp thành T0"; xem chuỗi quyết định tại `docs/decisions/index.md` dòng 28-32)
- `scripts/check-decision-citation-drift.mjs` + `test/scripts/check-decision-citation-drift.test.mjs` — quét `docs/backlog.md` + `docs/specs/*.md` tìm dòng còn trích một quyết định đã bị supersede mà không nhắc quyết định thay thế trên cùng dòng (STR72 CoS clause 2, PBI p-2d71dfc3); chỉ phát hiện, không tự sửa; spec: docs/specs/decision-citation-drift.md
- `scripts/check-decision-codes.mjs` + `test/scripts/check-decision-codes.test.mjs` — quét `test/**/*.test.mjs` tìm tên test còn nhúng mã quyết định nội bộ (str##/D#/RUL##/STR##/tsk-xxx) thay vì mô tả bất biến bằng lời thường (review-audit-self-decision.md mục Stable Code Artifacts); chặn (ratchet) chỉ vi phạm MỚI so với `scripts/check-decision-codes.baseline.json` đã chốt, không chặn ngược nợ cũ; `npm test` tự chạy qua glob `test/**/*.test.mjs`, không hook riêng
- `docs/id-systems-audit.md` — audit + quyết định hình dạng mọi hệ id/mã đang sống trong hệ thống (work.id/kind/Story/ADR/Rule/Contract phía fgOS; D-hex/D-local/cell-id/feature-slug/severity phía bee) — nguồn cho `work.id`'s `tsk-<hash>` và các migration STR53-STR58 (tất cả đã `done`); boundary appendix: `docs/architecture-map.md` Phụ lục B
- `bin/fgos.mjs` — CLI một cửa của work-state; chạy `node bin/fgos.mjs <verb>`; gồm verb `edit` — sửa đè các trường (title/kind/risk/verify/tier/refs/deps/acceptance/priority/intent — str7-str8-priority-intent) trên một item đã có, cùng cửa ghi CTR002 như `add`/`move`; gồm verb `take`/`return` — cửa pull giao–nhận việc cho tác nhân ngoài runner; gồm verb `pick` — cửa pull GỘP `take` + dựng workspace (`createWorktree`), role cố định `session`, không cờ `--role` (theo str83-fgos-slash-commands); gồm verb `review`/`approve`/`reject` — cổng duyệt PR nội bộ, một cổng cho mọi đề xuất `awaiting-approval`, nay leaf-vs-root-aware (con nhập vào nhánh của gốc, gốc nhập vào cây chính); `review`/`approve` nay chấp nhận thêm `--github [--pr <n>]` — vận chuyển thay thế CÙNG cổng duyệt qua GitHub thay vì diff/merge cục bộ (chỉ nguồn runner, theo github-adapter, spec: docs/specs/runner.md); gồm verb `catchup` — đồng bộ lại một việc đỗ vì gãy nhập/trôi tích hợp (spec: docs/specs/runner.md); gồm verb `session` (`start`/`end`/`list`) — vòng đời phiên checkout đa-phiên tùy chọn, mỗi phiên một worktree detached-HEAD cho cây nguồn, dùng chung MỘT kho `.fgos/` qua symlink (spec: docs/specs/runner.md); spec: docs/specs/work-state.md
- `src/state/` — lõi work-state: events (nhật ký; `appendEvent` nay chạy trong mutex nóng `state` (`withStateTx`, `src/state/hot-lock.mjs`) — xem spec Work-State RUL10 (tiền đề có ngưỡng — một người ghi tại một thời điểm; multi-agent ghi đồng thời qua mutex nóng `state`)), work (schema — STATUSES + STAGES + field `parent` lineage + field `domain`), fsm (bảng chuyển status + CAS), stage (bảng chuyển stage + CAS, chiều vĩ mô song song fsm; cạnh chuyển-stage tra theo domain của item — `coding`: `discovery → exploring → planning → executing`, trong đó phán-quyết `clear` ở `discovery` bỏ qua `exploring` để sang thẳng `planning` còn `unclear` đi qua `exploring`; tên `decompose` vẫn còn nhưng chỉ là bí danh legacy chỉ-để-rút-cạn (không việc MỚI nào vào được nữa); `synthetic`: một stage, không cạnh nào), domains (sổ đăng ký domain — stage list + step-mapping base-workflow + cạnh-chuyển mỗi domain; `coding` + ba domain minh họa/thử-nghiệm `synthetic` (đúng một stage), `triage`, `fixture-marketing`; base-workflow-model STR18, hoàn tất S1+S2), replay (fold), frontier (truy vấn sẵn-sàng — lọc theo status, stage domain-aware, VÀ lineage qua `parent`), dep-graph (dò chu trình trên `deps` — bất biến phi-chu-trình tại cửa ghi, per work-graph-intelligence S1), store (chủ ghi duy nhất + readRawEvents), envelope (phong bì output CTR001, `wrapEnvelope` — nay bọc MỌI verb ở một cửa in trong `bin/fgos.mjs main()`, STR37; spec: docs/specs/work-state.md §envelope)
- `src/cli/command-registry.mjs` — sổ verb máy-đọc của CLI (STR37, kernel, thuần dữ liệu): `SCHEMA_VERSION` + `COMMAND_REGISTRY` (mọi verb với `{name, invoke, description, parameters, examples, access read|mutation, deprecated}`); `bin/fgos.mjs` `--help [--json]` và `<verb> [<sub>] --help [--json]` sinh sổ từ đây; verb có sub-verb mang `subcommands`, `HELP_SELECTORS` (`--help`, `-h`) thành route của Rust host qua `scripts/export-command-selectors.mjs`; test chống-lệch `test/cli/fgos-manifest.test.mjs`, `test/cli/subcommand-flag-drift.test.mjs` (cờ handler ↔ schema sub-verb), `test/cli/fgos-verb-help-json.test.mjs`, `test/rust-host/help-routes.test.mjs` (qua host thật); spec: docs/specs/work-state.md §sổ verb
- `src/intake/classify.mjs` — logic thuần của `fgos submit`: deriveTitle, classify (tier/kind/risk cơ học), generateId (`tsk-<hash>` chống trùng, STR53)
- `src/intake/discovery.mjs` — context-discovery của stage `discovery` (stage đầu tiên của domain `coding`): `resolveDiscovery` (đọc-phán-ghi, dùng chung bởi verb `discover` và vòng tự hành) ĐÒI phán-quyết do người gọi cấp — judge lồng `judgeDiscovery` đã rút; phán-quyết `clear` chuyển item sang stage `planning`, `unclear` sang `exploring`
- `src/intake/plan.mjs` — phán chia-việc của stage `planning`: `resolvePlan` (đọc-phán-ghi, dùng chung bởi verb `plan` và vòng tự hành khi item ở stage `planning`, hoặc ở bí danh legacy `decompose`) ĐÒI phán-quyết do người gọi cấp — judge lồng `judgeDecompose` đã rút, cùng lý do `judgeDiscovery` rút; sinh con qua lineage `parent`, không qua `deps`
- `domains/coding/AGENTS.md` `## fgOS Workflow` + `.claude/skills/` (`.agents/skills/` mirror byte-identical) — lớp hướng dẫn P50: entry skill (`fgos-routing`) + skill giai đoạn (`fgos-coding-discovering`/`fgos-coding-exploring`/`fgos-coding-planning`/`fgos-coding-validating`/`fgos-coding-implement`/`fgos-coding-knowledge`) trỏ một phiên tự mở tới đúng skill theo `stage` của item; từ str89-fgos-domain-skills, tra cứu này domain-pluggable — đọc trường `domain` + `stage` của item rồi tra qua `skillForStage`/`getDomain` (`src/state/workflow-stage-graphs.mjs`), không còn giả định ngầm domain `coding`; `fgos-routing` nay có hàng khoá theo **status** `retrospective → fgos-coding-knowledge` (skill tổng hợp cấp nhãn Diataxis + soạn tài liệu người-dùng-cuối) — stage `compound-learn` đã rút, việc tổng hợp nó từng canh nay là việc của status `retrospective`; skill ĐỘC LẬP `fgos-submit-assist` (str51-llm-assist-classify) đã rút (tsk-6ar) — `/fgOS:submit` bước 6 (`plugins/fgOS/skills/submit/SKILL.md`) nay tự chạy clarify+classify trong cùng phiên sống, cùng việc mà skill đó từng làm nhưng trên bản mô tả SẠCH hơn; spec: docs/specs/work-state.md §RUL60 (hành vi), docs/specs/runner.md (lớp hướng dẫn)
- `plugins/fgOS/` (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` + `skills/<verb>/SKILL.md`) — bề mặt slash-command `/fgOS:<verb>` cho Claude Code, 12 verb wrapper (submit, pick, move, return, ask, answer, ready, stale, rollup, check, graph, conflicts), mỗi verb một wrapper one-door-write qua `bin/fgos.mjs <verb>`; spec: docs/specs/fgos-plugin.md
- `apps/fgos-gateway/` + `apps/fgos-gateway/web/` — fgos gateway (REST, MCP, bundle web dashboard nhúng sẵn; vòng đời `fgos gateway`) và bề mặt web dashboard: client trình duyệt ĐỘC LẬP (không phải code máy chủ trong gateway, theo tsk-7l9 + decision 0014); `herdr-dashboard/` là plugin herdr (TUI trong pane), `packages/herdr-fgos-common/rust` là adapter CLI fgos dùng chung của cả hai, gọi API REST/RPC của gateway từ ngoài; ba màn đọc (taskboard, task-detail, câu hỏi cần trả lời — phủ cả kênh `ask` lẫn `gate-approve`) cộng các hành động ghi đi qua verb một-cửa-ghi của fgOS (`answer`/`approve`/`add`/`edit`/`move`), không có đường ghi thứ hai; bật mặc định, port 8788, token bắt buộc; spec: docs/specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md (lớp UI/wireframe: docs/reference/herdr-web-dashboard-layout.md)
- `docs/how-to/`, `docs/tutorials/`, `docs/reference/`, `docs/explanation/` — tài liệu NGƯỜI-DÙNG-CUỐI theo bốn quadrant Diataxis (audience-facing, khác `docs/specs/` là BA-reference nội bộ); sinh bởi kỹ năng `fgos-coding-knowledge` ở status `retrospective` (grow-or-create một tài liệu SỐNG mỗi đường dẫn: gom mọi capture qua `fgos doc-sources` rồi tích luỹ không mất, ngăn Diataxis là trục cấu trúc duy nhất — write-side, spec: docs/specs/enduser-docs-authoring.md), quadrant khớp `docType` capture; `docs/explanation/` từ str64-backfill còn có 6 tài liệu chưng cất từ critical-patterns.md (learnings vận hành bee thật sự thuộc tiến trình hình thành fgOS); chỉ mục đọc-theo-tag máy-đọc-được: `docs/enduser-docs-index.json` (sinh bởi verb `fgos docs-index` / kỹ năng `fgos-indexing`, thay cho việc liệt-kê-tay từng tài liệu — supersedes con trỏ văn xuôi cũ, theo compound-learn-enduser-docs; ngăn `explanation` còn quét thêm `docs/decisions/` làm vị trí thay thế, theo str64-backfill); spec read-side: docs/specs/enduser-docs-index.md
- `src/runner/` + `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` — vòng tự hành (loop/dispatch/worktree/recovery/anti-loop/write-queue/root-affinity); `loop.mjs`'s `runWatch` + `write-queue.mjs`'s `onCommit` — chế độ `--watch` bền, tín hiệu-cơ-học + nghỉ dự phòng, ghép `runOnce` không đổi làm hộp đen (str7-str8-priority-intent, spec: docs/specs/runner.md §RUL53 (`--watch` — vòng cầm-giao bền, dừng chỉ khi có tín hiệu tường minh)); loop giao việc theo mẻ song song có giới hạn hai tầng (cấu hình `parallel` trong `.fgos/config.json`'s `runner` section, theo tsk-5vf), giữ quyền-sở-hữu-gốc trong một lượt chạy, quét làm-rõ rồi quét chia-việc trước mọi dispatch thi công; gặt-lại bỏ qua claim của cửa pull (`claimRole` human/session); `dispatch.mjs`'s executor là port có tên CTR009 v2 (`EXECUTOR_ADAPTERS`, per-tier qua config's `executors`, STR41), `ensureRunnerConfigForDir` tự sinh cấu hình mặc định tại `.fgos/config.json` khi vắng mặt (không áp dụng cho `--config` tường minh, str76-runner-bootstrap; tsk-5hv xoá hẳn fallback về file flat legacy cũ); worker của loop và fan-out chạy như một Unit run qua `runUnit` (`work-dispatch.mjs`'s `spawnWorker`), `fgos-runner` không còn `--config` (spec: docs/specs/runner.md §RUL93 (the runner loop's worker and the fan-out batch run as one Unit run each)) và prompt worker được tách sang `prompt-templates.mjs` + `prompt-templates/*.txt` (chọn template qua bảng cơ học kind/tier/domain, substitution `{placeholder}` thuần, log dispatch kèm tên+hash template, STR49); `goal-check.mjs` — hàm goal-check dùng chung giữa vòng tự hành và verb `return`; `write-queue.mjs` — cửa ghi tuần tự giữ một-người-ghi dưới song song; `root-affinity.mjs` — quyền-sở-hữu-gốc, giữ mọi con của một gốc chung một chủ trong một lượt chạy; `resolveRepoRoot` nay còn xác nhận HEAD repo resolve được trước khi runner claim bất kỳ item nào (fail-fast, str86-runner-headless-git D ecfd0d1a); config: `.fgos/config.json`'s `runner` section (tự sinh khi vắng mặt tại đường mặc định, nguồn config duy nhất kể từ tsk-5hv); spec: docs/specs/runner.md
- `docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` + `src/runner/dispatch/confinement/` — Agent Confinement Authority: runtime one-door confinement enforcement (`executeThroughConfinement`), machine backend registry `~/.fgos/confinement-backends.json`, local `bwrap` v1 driver with 8 falsification probes, required fail-closed checks, attestation storage (`confinement-attestation.v1`), herdr convergence with shared `evaluateBypassPairing`, setup defaults and doctor checks; spec: docs/specs/confinement-authority.md Pane herdr confine cho agent không phải claude (codex/agy/pi): công thức private-home + account inventory + lịch sử các commit đã đi qua (và vì sao từng bị quên) ở §13.1.
- `docs/architect/README.md` + `docs/architect/architecture-intent.md` + `docs/architect/domainization/README.md` — portal architect-level, registry intention xuyên-khu-vực, và deep-dive domainization (core đóng vs `domains/<name>/` adapter mở: manifest/workflow YAML, task-spec, skill, knowledge, doctrine, agent, resolver, enforcement); active thread đầu tiên giữ intent mở rộng fgOS từ fan-out/fan-in + artifact mediation thành năng lực group-thinking/problem-solving rộng hơn (Delphi/NGT/RFC/adversarial/master-coordinator), giữ `group-cognition-framework.yaml` isolation-heavy không bị nới ngầm; liên quan Step 09 group-thinking substrate, Step 10 coding-domain adoption, component authority boundary map, và Domain Components And Extension Layer
- `src/workflow/` (`definition.mjs`, `guide-schema.mjs`, `loader.mjs`, `runner.mjs` = Playbook proposer, `units-source.mjs`; case model: `case-projection.mjs` pure fold, `case-admission.mjs` admission predicate, `case-admission-port.mjs` port implementation, `case-bindings.mjs` worktree bindings, `case-runtime.mjs` reservation/settle/gate-answer files, `case-frame.mjs` nested frame, `case-lock.mjs` `advance` hold, `case-start.mjs`, `case-verbs.mjs` start/status/answer/resume/close, `case-close.mjs`; `unit-handoff.mjs`, `ref-digests.mjs`, `store.mjs` ledger) + `src/runner/execution/case-admission-port.mjs` (port contract owned by the Execution Core) + `core/workflows/*.yaml` — Workflow engine: guide + case ledger, admission, human gates, Playbook proposer; `units-source.mjs` dịch units file của `fgos workflow start --units` thành Workflow tạm (RUL89 (workflow start --units)); spec: `docs/specs/runner.md`
- `docs/specs/workflow.md` — spec khu vực Workflow (owner duyệt 2026-10-19, D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger); lane AGENT-WF): workflow là guide (hướng dẫn tác nghiệp + ràng buộc MUST/SHOULD/MAY instead), không phải kịch bản; Workflow case là ledger duy nhất admit activity do agent đề xuất và ghi tiến độ; milestone gắn subject, khung được duyệt, ràng buộc authority fail-closed (N1), catalog MUST đóng, ví dụ trước → sau; supersede một phần 0048 §2 và 0049 §4 của `docs/specs/runner.md`
- `src/runner/execution/` (`unit.mjs`, `bind.mjs`, `run.mjs`, `patterns/`) — Execution Core (Request-to-Run P1/P2/P4): Unit (hợp đồng dữ liệu duy nhất), `bind()` (chọn executor 5 mức), `fgos run` (cửa chạy mới, herdr mặc định), CollaborationPattern (`solo`, `reviewed`, `panel` + presets `consult`, `research-fan-out`, `rfc`, `code-change`); `src/runner/dispatch/write-scope.mjs` — matcher duy nhất của phạm vi ghi Unit (RUL84 (one write-scope matcher)), dùng cho runner commit, settlement và Workflow; spec: `docs/specs/runner.md`

# Agent Mailbox Component Specification

```txt
Document type: BA-grade area specification
Audience: Human reviewer, maintainer, implementation agent
Purpose: Define how a message from one agent session reaches another live agent session in time on one machine, with an honest delivery report, and without any message ever carrying the user's authority. Later parts (acknowledgement, expiry, cross-machine, the typed nudge for an idle agy session) are recorded in section 15 and are not part of the first slice.
Design status: Draft proposal; not signed. At gate G0 the owner signs the scope and bounds of V-013, the architecture (pure core crate, ports Nudge and Presence, snapshot record under a mutex, native `hook mailbox` kind of the existing hook door; no terminal access and no shared terminal crate in the first slice) and the semantics (states recorded, offered, refused; wake as the sender's permission; names `<project>-<cli>-<2 characters>`; per-process generation; head only; no durable sessions; same project only). The owner does not sign the numeric values (all are configuration keys), the claim that peer input never acts as user input (mitigated, measured in print mode only, not proven), the hook cost in each CLI's real hook environment, the cross-component prerequisites of section 14, or the later parts of section 15. Narrowed to the first slice by owner decision A on 2026-10-19; revised after council round 2, an independent architecture panel, an authority and boundary review, and further measurements (section 17); the V-011 narrowing accepted on 2026-10-20 as V-013; the typed nudge and its supporting chain moved to a later part on 2026-10-20 (section 15.8). The delivery plan became a verification ladder, the Codex adapter got a stop rule and an authorization prerequisite, and `codex queue` on a busy session joined S0 (owner, 2026-10-20; section 14). Open for the owner: section 16 questions 11 and 16 (question 16 is now a prerequisite of the Codex adapter, not of G0) and the recommended-pending rows of section 17.
Implementation status: Not started
Canonical: No (becomes canonical when signed)

Owner: Agent Mailbox component (proposed)
Source (planned): packages/mailbox/contracts; packages/mailbox/rust/{core,store} (crates fgos-mailbox-core and fgos-mailbox); thin wiring in apps/fgos/src/wiring/. No shared terminal crate in the first slice (section 15.8)
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20
Supersedes: nothing. It asks the owner to narrow V-011 (section 2).

```txt
Document type: BA-grade area specification
Audience: Human reviewer, maintainer, implementation agent
Purpose: Define how a message from one agent session reaches another live agent session in time on one machine, with an honest delivery report, and without any message ever carrying the user's authority. Later parts (acknowledgement, expiry, cross-machine, the typed nudge for an idle agy session) are recorded in section 15 and are not part of the first slice.
Design status: Draft proposal; not signed. At gate G0 the owner signs the scope and bounds of V-013, the architecture (pure core crate, ports Nudge and Presence, snapshot record under a mutex, native `hook mailbox` kind of the existing hook door; no terminal access and no shared terminal crate in the first slice) and the semantics (states recorded, offered, refused; wake as the sender's permission; names `<project>-<cli>-<2 characters>`; per-process generation; head only; no durable sessions; same project only). The owner does not sign the numeric values (all are configuration keys), the claim that peer input never acts as user input (mitigated, measured in print mode only, not proven), the hook cost in each CLI's real hook environment, the cross-component prerequisites of section 14, or the later parts of section 15. Narrowed to the first slice by owner decision A on 2026-10-19; revised after council round 2, an independent architecture panel, an authority and boundary review, and further measurements (section 17); the V-011 narrowing accepted on 2026-10-20 as V-013; the typed nudge and its supporting chain moved to a later part on 2026-10-20 (section 15.8). The delivery plan became a verification ladder, the Codex adapter got a stop rule and an authorization prerequisite, and `codex queue` on a busy session joined S0 (owner, 2026-10-20; section 14). Open for the owner: section 16 questions 11 and 16 (question 16 is now a prerequisite of the Codex adapter, not of G0) and the recommended-pending rows of section 17.
Implementation status: Not started
Canonical: No (becomes canonical when signed)

Owner: Agent Mailbox component (proposed)
Source (planned): packages/mailbox/contracts; packages/mailbox/rust/{core,store} (crates fgos-mailbox-core and fgos-mailbox); thin wiring in apps/fgos/src/wiring/. No shared terminal crate in the first slice (section 15.8)

docs/platform/agent-mailbox/spec.md.sectionText:
## 2. Why this exists, and the V-011 gate

`V-011` says the foundation core does not require "a general mailbox" and that new persisted entities need "a distinct authority, recovery need, or invariant that existing entities cannot represent correctly". This spec does **not** propose a general mailbox. It does not claim a recovery need either, because nothing in the first slice outlives its machine's local record.

| V-011 test | Claim for the first slice |
|---|---|
| Distinct authority | Delivery: only this component decides whether, when and how a message enters a live agent's context. Five CLIs differ, three lose or hold a message silently in common situations, and nothing reports delivery honestly |
| Recovery need | **Not claimed.** It returns with the later parts (section 15) and is argued again then |
| Invariant | A message from another agent is peer input, never user input, and never carries permission. One place must enforce this, or every adapter must |

The owner accepted this narrowed claim on 2026-10-20 and it is recorded as V-013 in the agent coordination vision (`docs/architect/agent-coordination/vision.md` and its platform copy); V-011 is not edited. V-013 covers the first slice only. The later parts of section 15 are open to be added, each with its own argument under V-011's three tests (recovery need above all) and its own owner decision.

Council round 1 found no named consumer yet (question 3). The first slice is the part that can be used without one: honest delivery of a message into a live herdr or terminal session.

docs/platform/agent-mailbox/spec.md.text: ## 3. Vocabulary
docs/platform/agent-mailbox/spec.md.sectionText:
## 3. Vocabulary

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Session | One live agent conversation. It has a stable identity from `docs/platform/session-identity/spec.md`. In this spec "session" means that, never a worktree-session of `src/runner/session.mjs`; "the CLI's own session file" is the file a CLI keeps for its running process |
| Address | An entry in the mailbox registry for one live session on this machine, valid for that session's lifetime and released when it ends (section 5.1). Addresses that outlive a session are not part of the first slice (section 15.5). People and agents type its short name; the key is never typed (section 5.1.1) |
| Message | An immutable envelope (section 5.1) addressed to exactly one address |
| Checkpoint | The boundary between two steps of an agent where input may safely be inserted |
| Drain | A recipient-side claim of its pending messages at a checkpoint, printing their frames, then a conditional finish (section 5.2). It is the work of the `mailbox` kind of `fgos hook`, not a verb |
| Offered | A message whose frame the claiming process emitted on the harness's output channel. It is not proof that the model read it |
| Attempt token | A value issued at claim; the finish of that claim must present it, together with the binding generation |
| Nudge | A one-line signal that wakes an idle session and tells it to read its mail; never the body |
| Wake | Start a new turn on an idle session |
| Tier | How fast the adapter can reach a session: `push`, `turn` or `pull` (section 6.2) |
| Delivery report | The answer a sender gets: a state plus one sentence saying when the recipient will see the message |
| Peer input | Text that came from another agent. Always labelled as such inside the context |
| Chain depth | The number of reply links from a message back to the first message of its exchange |
| Human input | A prompt typed by a person into the session, as opposed to a message from another agent |

docs/platform/agent-mailbox/spec.md.sample: 4. Architecture
docs/platform/agent-mailbox/spec.md.text: ## 4. Architecture
docs/platform/agent-mailbox/spec.md.sectionText:
## 4. Architecture

The component is hexagonal (design principle 3): a pure core, driving verbs, two outbound ports, a local record and thin drivers.

```txt
 driving side (who calls the mailbox)
   fgos mailbox send|inbox|list|status        hooks (receiver side)
                                              fgos hook mailbox --event ...
        \                                       /
         v                                      v
   +-----------------------------------------------+
   |   verbs and the hook kind (thin wiring)       |
   |                                               |
   |   CORE (fgos-mailbox-core, pure)              |
   |   envelope, state machine, policies, names    |
   |   (takes `now` and an id source)              |
   |                                               |
   |   record adapter (module, not a port)         |
   |   outbound ports:   Nudge     Presence        |
   +-----------------------------------------------+
                           |          |
                           v          v
                 codex queue / Claude  hook events / the CLI's own
                 session socket        session file / the registry
```

Rules. Rules 1 and 3 are enforced by the dependency set of `fgos-mailbox-core` (Cargo: it depends on nothing but serde, so it cannot import an adapter or do I/O). Rule 2 and the layer direction are held by review. `test/architecture.test.mjs` scans only `.mjs` files under `src` and `bin`, so the architecture manifest cannot express a Rust crate boundary (this answers question 7); no workspace-wide cargo dependency test is proposed in this slice.

1. The core imports no adapter and no tool name (no `git`, `herdr`, `claude`, `codex`, `pi`, `omp`, `agy`); it holds `cli` as an opaque string. Lower layers never know upper layers; adapters adapt to the core.
2. Each port has one authority. The core decides policy; an adapter only moves a signal.
3. The core takes the current time and an id source as parameters and performs no I/O. This also makes the storm and loop tests of rung V1 deterministic.
4. Add through the door, not beside it (L10). The first slice touches no terminal and reads no screen; if a typed nudge is added later it goes through the existing doors (terminal-control and agent-protocol, section 15.8), not through a mechanism of its own. Process identity and liveness are `fgos-process` (section 5.1). Atomic file replacement goes through `durable-file`, mutual exclusion through `holder-lock`. Hook installation goes through `src/setup/agent-hooks.mjs`, and the hook entry is the existing `fgos hook` door. Instruction text goes through the instruction registry. The mailbox adds none of these mechanisms again.
5. A port is added only when a second real implementation exists or a swap has been shown to be needed (section 11). `Nudge` has three real implementations in the first slice (Claude Code, Codex, agy) and is a port. `Presence` reads the CLI's own session file status, hook events and the registry, and is a port because its authority must be single. The record adapter has one implementation and is a plain module; `MailStore` and `Replication` return as ports with section 15.2.

Dependency direction. The mailbox sits at L4, beside the run supervisor and above the shared primitives it uses. In the first slice it imports `fgos-process`, `fgos-holder-lock`, `fgos-durable-file` and `fgos-session-identity` only, and nothing from agent-protocol or terminal-control; a later typed nudge adds those two (section 15.8). It never imports the run supervisor, the Event Store, git, observe or any Workflow code. Nothing below it imports it; only `apps/fgos` wiring and tests do.

docs/platform/agent-mailbox/spec.md.sample: 4.1 Layout and language
docs/platform/agent-mailbox/spec.md.text: ### 4.1 Layout and language
docs/platform/agent-mailbox/spec.md.sectionText:
### 4.1 Layout and language

| Layer | Language | Path |
|---|---|---|
| Core (pure, no I/O: envelope, state machine, policies, name resolution, framing) | Rust | `packages/mailbox/rust/core` (crate `fgos-mailbox-core`; dependency: serde only) |
| Record adapter, ports wiring, verbs, hook kind, adapters | Rust | `packages/mailbox/rust/store` (crate `fgos-mailbox`, added to the workspace `Cargo.toml`): record, ports, `adapters/{claude,codex,agy}.rs`. An adapter holds only what no other component holds: the hook payload shape of its CLI, a wake channel that needs no terminal (`codex queue`, the Claude socket), and how to find the head process and its version |
| Contracts, versioned adapter table | JSON | `packages/mailbox/contracts/` including `adapters.v1.json` |
| Verbs `fgos mailbox send\|inbox\|list\|status` | Rust, thin wiring, no logic | `apps/fgos/src/wiring/mailbox_*.rs` |
| Hook entry `fgos hook mailbox` | Rust, native kind of the existing door | `apps/fgos` (prerequisite in section 14) |
| Hook install and its doctor probe | Node (legacy-node), existing | `src/setup/agent-hooks.mjs`: new hook kind `mailbox`; `commandIsKind` extended for the new event option |
| Instruction text | Markdown | one contract file under `packages/mailbox/contracts/` renders the frame; an optional standing line lives in `components/agent-mailbox/instructions/peer-input.md` (section 5.5) |
| Extension for pi and omp (later part) | TypeScript | the only form those CLIs accept |

Every path in this table under `packages/mailbox`, `apps/fgos/src/wiring/mailbox_*.rs` and `components/agent-mailbox` is planned; none exists yet.

Adapters stay inside the `fgos-mailbox` crate until an outside consumer exists. Each adapter reads its tested versions from `adapters.v1.json` (`tested_against: {cli, version}`); it pins hook, socket and queue behaviour. When the version of the receiving process is not one of the tested ones the adapter turns off every nudge path not verified at that version (tier `push` falls back to `turn`) and the delivery report says so. The hook drain keeps running at an untested version, and the delivery report names the version as untested. The version is the target process's own (Claude Code records it in its session file; several versions can run at once after an update), and where a CLI does not record it the installed version is used and the delivery report says so. Section 6.2 already allows lowering a tier and forbids raising it without proof.

**The hook door (owner decision 2026-10-20).** The hook entry is `fgos hook mailbox --event <stop|post-tool-use|...>` through the project shim: a native kind of the existing `fgos hook` door. There is no second door `fgos mailbox drain`. Today `hook` is entirely legacy-node (`packages/host-runtime/contracts/command-routes.json`: selector `hook`, route kind `legacy-cli`, payload `legacy-node`; `apps/fgos/src/legacy_exec.rs` runs it), and the other two kinds, `dispatch-decide` and `decision-question`, run only on `Agent|Task` and `AskUserQuestion` events, not on the hot path. The prerequisite (section 14) is that the host handles `hook` with native code: it takes the `mailbox` kind in Rust and hands every other kind to the legacy-node payload. Porting `dispatch-decide` or `decision-question` to Rust is not proposed (the first pulls a large part of `bind.mjs` and `config.mjs`, and neither is on the hot path). docs/platform/agent-mailbox/spec.md.title: 5.1 Address and envelope
docs/platform/agent-mailbox/spec.md.sample: 5.1 Address and envelope
docs/platform/agent-mailbox/spec.md.text: ### 5.1 Address and envelope
docs/platform/agent-mailbox/spec.md.sectionText:
### 5.1 Address and envelope

An **address** is an entry in a small registry that is part of the record snapshot (section 6.4). It maps to at most one live session. A binding is the tuple `(address, generation, native handle, process identity)`. The native handle is the session's own channel (Claude pid and socket, Codex thread id); a later typed nudge would add a terminal-control key (section 15.8). The Codex thread id reaches a hook in its payload and, per `docs/platform/session-identity/spec.md`, a shell command in `CODEX_THREAD_ID`; a session for which neither is available has no handle and the adapter says `pull`. A session that ends leaves its address; the next session that takes the same name gets a new generation (below) and receives only messages written for that generation, so a stale instruction is never replayed into a stranger. The address does not outlive its session in this slice (durable sessions are recorded as not done in section 15.5). Whether the registration side and the `send` side derive the same key from their environments is not measured (the hook process's environment in each CLI is unverified).

**Registration and generation (owner decision 2026-10-20).** The checkpoint hook or extension registers the head the first time it runs in a process: writer id and the head's process identity. A `send` to a name with no registered head is refused as an unknown address.

*Process identity.* The binding carries the head's process identity as an `fgos_process::Record` (host, boot id, pid namespace, pid, start time) and "is this head gone" is `fgos_process::judge` (`packages/process/rust/src/facts.rs`); the mailbox compares no pid or start time itself, and the boot id keeps a reboot from making an old record look like the same head. A generation bumps when the registering head's `Record` differs from the stored one or when the stored one is judged `Dead`. `Unknown` never bumps and never releases an address. *Whose pid the head is* is decided by the adapter of its CLI (the CLI's own session file records pid, start time and version where it has one); the hook's own pid is never used, and the terminal root that session-identity returns when no env id exists (for agy) is not the head.

The generation is keyed on the process, not on the conversation: a `--resume` makes a new process and therefore a new generation, so mail written for the old process is not replayed, which fits the decision that there are no durable sessions. Registration still happens once per process, in the hook or extension. The generation is bumped inside the same `holder-lock` mutex hold that installs the new snapshot, in the same write that records the new binding, so two heads registering at once cannot take the same number and no separate generation file exists. A message records the generation of its recipient at `send` (`to_generation`); claim and finish succeed only while it equals the address's current generation, and a claim or finish made by an older head is ignored. Mail of an older generation is never offered again.

**`from` is attribution, not authority.** The sender identity is what session-identity returns for the caller (section 5.1.1). It is not authenticated: any process that can run `fgos mailbox send` in a shell gets some identity. `from` therefore only names who is accountable for a message. It never grants a human slot, an exemption from a policy or a budget reset.

**What holds an address (agreed by the owner on 2026-10-20; the research of the same day found nothing against it):** a terminal pane together with the head of the CLI process running in it. The first slice reaches the head through hooks, which need no terminal, so a tmux pane or a bare tty is served the same way. A subagent or an in-process teammate inside that CLI is never addressed: a message reaches the head, which decides whether to pass it on (section 15.6). The external channels measured so far (socket, `codex queue`, the extensions, and the typed signal of section 15.8) reach the head of a CLI in a terminal. A hook can reach one Claude Code subagent on its own: `additionalContext` returned for an event that carries a subagent's `agent_id` landed only in that subagent's context (measured 2026-10-20, section 15.6). That is a technical possibility that the mailbox declines on principle (section 15.6). The record is per project (section 6.4), because fgOS runs on many projects on one machine; a machine address is not part of this slice (section 15.2).

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `id` | opaque unique string assigned by the component. Later, new messages may carry an event hash instead; the format is not part of the contract |
| `from` | address of the sending session, set by the component from the caller's own identity, never accepted from message text. Attribution only (above) |
| `to` | address of exactly one session, resolved from a name (section 5.1.1). Agents may not address a group |
| `to_generation` | the generation of the recipient's address at the moment of `send`, set by the component, never by the caller |
| `reply_to` | id of the message this one answers. **Derived by the component** (section 5.4); a value supplied by the caller is only a hint and is refused unless that message was offered to the sender |
| `depth` | chain depth, stored at append time so pruning an ancestor never changes it |
| `wake` | boolean, default `false`. The sender's permission, not a claim about the recipient's state and not a mark of urgency: `true` means "if the recipient is idle, you may start a new turn on it so it reads this". The component checks the recipient's state at `send` and the delivery report reports what happened (woken through a named channel with an expected delay; recipient busy, so it sees the message at its next checkpoint whatever `wake` says; or state unknown, so nobody is woken). A busy recipient is never interrupted and `wake` does not make a message arrive sooner. Subject to section 5.3 |
| `kind` | `message` (a recipient may reply) or `notice` (machine-made, from the system address; never replied to, never counted by the loop guard, never wakes) |
| `body` | plain text, size capped (section 5.3), immutable once written and stored apart from the snapshot (section 6.4). Content longer than the cap is sent as a path or link the receiver reads with its own authority |
| `recorded_at` | time stamped by the recording process. All windows, TTLs and queue ages use it. There is no sender time in this slice |

`reply_by` is reserved for the later parts and is refused in the first slice.

docs/platform/agent-mailbox/spec.md.sample: 5.1.1 Names
docs/platform/agent-mailbox/spec.md.sectionText:
### 5.1.1 Names

Confirmed by the owner on 2026-10-20 (shape and same-project delivery).

- **Key.** The writer id within the project's record; the project is the record's own location (section 6.4), so no project key exists or is invented. The writer id is what session-identity returns (`docs/platform/session-identity/spec.md`): a UUID for Claude Code, Codex and pi; `att-<attemptId>` for a runner worker (section 5a of that spec); the terminal root pid for a head that has no id, such as agy, until it registers. Verified in that spec: env ids are tried in the order `FGOS_SESSION_ID`, `CODEX_THREAD_ID`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, and the fallback is the highest ancestor with a terminal. omp exports no id of its own and neither CLI is read by session-identity today (section 16 question 2), so pi and omp stay later parts. The key is never typed by a person.
- **Short name.** Owner feedback 2026-10-20: short enough to type; the project as a prefix so names are unique across projects on the machine; the CLI in the name because work crosses CLIs; and an id when two collide. Shape `<project>-<cli>-<2 characters>`, the project folder name, the CLI (`claude`, `codex`, `agy`, `pi`, `omp`) and two hex characters, three on a collision within that project and CLI. Examples: `forgent-claude-2b`, `forgent-codex-9c`, `forgent-agy-4e`, `forgent-pi-1a`, `mdview-claude-1a`. Claude Code already names its sessions `<project folder>-<2 characters>` (its session file records `name` with `nameSource: derived`, for example `forgent-2b`, and `SendMessage` addresses `@name`), so a Claude head keeps its own two characters and the mailbox name is `forgent-claude-2b`; a Claude name whose source is `auto` is free text with spaces and is not used. Heads of the other CLIs take two characters not yet used by that project and CLI. Resolution accepts the exact name, else a unique prefix of a name, so `forgent-codex` reaches the only Codex head of the project and is refused with the candidates listed when there are several. The full key, or a unique prefix of it, is the unambiguous fallback, shown by `list --long`. Delivery across projects is not in the first slice (the record is per project, section 6.4); the names are already unique across projects so it can be added later. Confirmed by the owner on 2026-10-20 (shape, CLI in the name, same-project delivery in the first slice).
- **Role aliases** such as `coordinator` are a later addition and not part of the first slice.
- **Resolution.** Exact short name first, then a unique prefix of a short name, then a unique key prefix. An ambiguous or unknown name is refused, with the candidates listed in the refusal. A name is never taken from message text.

docs/platform/agent-mailbox/spec.md.sample: 5.2 States
docs/platform/agent-mailbox/spec.md.text: ### 5.2 States
docs/platform/agent-mailbox/spec.md.sectionText:
### 5.2 States

```txt
refused at send: answered in the send output, nothing is recorded

recorded --claim(attempt token, generation)--> in-flight --emit, then finish(token, generation)--> offered
    ^                                              |
    +---- deadline passed, offer count + 1 -------+
recorded --older than record TTL--> refused (notice)
in-flight --offers exceed the cap--> refused (notice)
```

| State | Meaning | Who moves it |
|---|---|---|
| `recorded` | in the snapshot (section 6.4), not yet offered | `send` |
| `in-flight` | a drain or `inbox --claim` claimed it; carries an attempt token, a deadline, an offer count and the claiming head's generation | the claiming process |
| `offered` | the claiming process emitted the frame on the harness's output channel and then finished the claim | `finish` |
| `refused` | policy refused it, with a reason | `send` (synchronously) or the lazy sweep below |

**Claim, emit, finish.** One process does all three. Under the snapshot mutex it claims and gets an attempt token; outside the mutex it emits the frame; under the mutex again it finishes, and the finish succeeds only if the message is still `in-flight`, the token matches and the binding generation is still current. A finish that fails changes nothing; the frame was already emitted. **Duplicate window, stated plainly:** if the process dies or is killed after emit and before finish, if the finish loses the mutex within its budget, or if the deadline passed and another claim took the message, the same message is offered again and the recipient sees it twice. The frame says a repeat is possible and carries `attempt` (section 5.5). The component never claims exactly-once, and `offered` never claims that the model read the frame: only that this component put it on the harness's channel.

There is no daemon, so no process wakes when a deadline passes. **The deadline is evaluated lazily** by whichever process reads next (a drain, an `inbox --claim`, a `send` to that address, or `status`): an in-flight message past its deadline returns to `recorded` with its offer count raised, and when the count passes the cap it becomes `refused`. A message can therefore sit `in-flight` past its deadline until someone reads; `status` shows it. The same sweep applies the record TTL.

Three things must never be confused: *recorded* (written), *offered* (emitted toward the model's context by the harness's channel), *handled* (acted on). The first slice knows the first two only. A sender's `send` returns `recorded` plus the delivery report of section 6.2 and never claims more. Measured: Claude Code returns `success:true` to a sender even when the receiver holds the message behind a dialog. Monotonic means one total order `recorded < in-flight < offered`, with `in-flight` allowed to step back to `recorded` only through the sweep.

`held` (approval by a person) is cut from this slice: it has no approver, no verb and no consumer. It returns in section 15.1 together with an `approve` verb.

docs/platform/agent-mailbox/spec.md.sample: 5.3 Policies (core, adapter-independent)
docs/platform/agent-mailbox/spec.md.text: ### 5.3 Policies (core, adapter-independent)
docs/platform/agent-mailbox/spec.md.sectionText:
### 5.3 Policies (core, adapter-independent)

Starting values come from the reference implementation studied (reason-network, `src/daemon/mail.rs`) and from council rounds 1 and 2. They are **unmeasured on fgOS** and live in the config registry (section 12), not in code constants. Rung V1 replays them with a scripted storm and loop test, and rung V6 measures them with real agents; the owner does not sign the numbers (section 14, G0).

**What these limits are.** They protect the mailbox's own channel and are defaults owned here. They are not communication authorization: who may address whom, and the budget a case or a Unit may spend on messages, belong to the coordination foundation (the Vision lists communication authorization and loop bounds among its responsibilities; V-013 does not narrow that) and would reach this component through one policy input (`allow` or `deny(reason)`, plus a send budget), the same shape as the Execution Core's `CaseAdmissionPort` (`src/runner/execution/case-admission-port.mjs`). No implementation of that input exists for live messages today: the nearest are `anti-loop.mjs` (visits of Work) and `maxRounds` of the reviewed pattern, neither of which covers a message between two heads. In the first slice the input is absent and every head of the project may address every other (section 16 question 16 asks who authorizes a sender).

**What actually brakes a loop.** Chain depth counts only explicitly linked reply chains: the derived link (section 5.4) needs a message offered to the sender from the recipient. It does not stop a cycle in which each hop is a fresh message, for example A to B, B to C, C to A, A to B, and so on: every hop has no linked parent, so depth stays 0 and no ordered pair reaches the pair cap quickly. An earlier draft claimed depth stops any cycle; that claim is struck, and the cycle above is a core test (section 11). The brakes are the session budget, the rolling window, the queue cap, the record TTL and the lifetime cap. Depth and the pair guard are backstops for linked replies and pairs.

**Evidence on loops (2026-10-20, `plans/reports/research-261020-1814-mailbox-real-agent-loop-test.md`).** With real agents the quotas were insurance that was never exercised: in 50 runs of Claude Code `haiku` over four scenarios, quotas off and on, every run stopped on its own, the longest at 4 messages and 5 turns, and no quota ever came due. An FYI was answered in 0 of 15 runs; a task handoff was answered in 12 of 15 and declined in 3 because the task was outside the receiver's user task. A scripted pair with no model, always replying "thanks" with `wake`, ran to its end with quotas off and was stopped with quotas on: the wake quota at message 6, chain depth at 8, the lifetime wake cap at 101. In 14 of 14 forced refusals (thresholds lowered) the agent's turn ended with no retry and no direct write to the inbox, but the refusal text itself says do not retry, so this is not evidence the agent would refrain without that text. Limits: 5 runs per cell, one model, `--wake` was written into the frame's reply command in the test (the worst case, where every reply wakes), and the scratch runs sat inside the repository. The quotas stay as insurance; no real runaway has ever exercised them.

| Policy | Rule | Starting value |
|---|---|---|
| Size | refuse over the cap, tell the sender to send a path or link | 16 KiB (reference: 64 KiB) |
| Chain depth | refuse a `message` deeper than the cap. Counted on the derived chain, so it bounds linked reply chains only (see above) | 6 |
| Session budget | agent-origin `send`s by one session inside the rolling window (section 5.4); past the cap refuse. Refused attempts count too | 20 |
| Lifetime cap | `send`s by one session over its whole life (per generation), never reset. It is the only brake that does not depend on a reset, and it is mandatory because the rolling window is the only reset on every CLI in this slice (section 5.4) | 200 (a placeholder; unmeasured) |
| Loop guard | `message`s between one ordered pair inside a window; past the cap refuse with "this looks like a loop, check with your user". No sender is exempt: `from` is not authenticated | 12 per 10 minutes |
| Group guard | an agent addressing a group is refused | always |
| Wake quota per exchange | messages between one unordered pair of heads form an **exchange** while the gap between two consecutive messages is below the gap value; a longer silence starts a new exchange and its counter starts at zero. Within one exchange at most K `wake:true` sends, both directions together, take effect. Past K the message is still recorded and only the wake is dropped, and **the delivery report says so** ("the wake quota of this exchange is used up; it will see this at its next checkpoint"). Nothing is refused for this reason, because a lost message is worse than a late one | gap 600 s, K = 5 (placeholders; unmeasured) |
| Wake lifetime cap | `wake:true` sends that took effect, by one session (per its generation) to one recipient, never reset by anything. The last brake for a loop slower than the exchange gap; a long-lived coordinator that reaches it sees it in `status`, and a new generation starts again | 50 (a placeholder; unmeasured) |
| Queue cap | maximum pending per recipient, with a per-sender share. When full the **newest** is refused; an old legitimate message is never evicted. No slot is reserved for a "human" sender, because a sender cannot prove it is one | 50 total, 10 per sender |
| Record TTL | a message still `recorded` after this age becomes `refused` with a notice, by the lazy sweep. Headers (id, from, to, reply_to, depth, state, times, wake) are kept for the loop window plus the depth horizon; bodies of `offered` and `refused` messages are dropped after the body retention | 24 h; bodies 7 d |
| Redelivery | an in-flight message not finished by its deadline is offered again, at most this many offers, then refused with a notice | 3 offers |
| Trust class | every message from another session is `peer`; it never carries user authority and passes the framing of section 5.5 | always |

**Refusals at `send` are returned in the verb's own output and are not recorded as messages**, so they need no asynchronous notice. They are counted: refusals per reason and nudge outcomes are **bounded counters inside the per-address snapshot** (a fixed number of keys, oldest evicted), never one file or one entry per refusal, so a flood of refused sends cannot grow the record. A `notice` is created only when the system refuses a message that was already recorded (record TTL, redelivery cap). Notices live in a separate lane per address with their own small cap; the oldest notice is dropped when it overflows; at most one notice per (sender, reason) per window; a notice that cannot be delivered is dropped with a counter and never noticed again. A notice says "do not retry; ask your user".
